header.running_head: Weeping Over the Deaths of Elders

blocks.text: drank). At this, Hadhrat Suhayb (RA) cried out, "O poor Umar! O my dear brother! Who is there for us after him?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Take it easy, dear brother. Don't you know that the person over whom people cry loudly will be punished?"

Narrating from his father, Hadhrat Abu Burdah narrates that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) was stabbed, Hadhrat Suhayb (RA) arrived weeping in a loud voice. "Is it over me that you weep?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) enquired. When Hadhrat Suhayb (RA) replied that it was, Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Don't you know that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'The person over whom people cry (loudly) shall be punished'?"

Hadhrat Miqdaam bin Ma'dikarib (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) was wounded, (his daughter) Hadhrat Hafsah (RA) entered the room saying, "O companion of Rasulullaah ﷺ! O father-in-law of Rasulullaah ﷺ! O Ameerul Mu'mineen!" Hadhrat Umar (RA) said to his son, "O Abdullaah (RA)! Help me to sit up because I cannot tolerate what I am hearing." When Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) supported Hadhrat Umar (RA) against his chest, Hadhrat Umar (RA) said to Hadhrat Hafsah (RA), "By the rights that I have over you, I prohibit you from wailing over me after this. I have of course no control over your eyes (for you are allowed to weep as much as you please). Whenever a deceased person is praised for what was not in him, the angels record this (against him)."[^1]
Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Zaid (RA) and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) Weep at the Death of Hadhrat Umar (RA)

Hadhrat Abdul Malik bin Zaid narrates from his father that as he was weeping, someone once asked Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Zaid (RA), "What makes you weep, O Abu A'war?" Hadhrat Sa'eed (RA) replied, "I am weeping over the fate of Islaam. It has sustained a void at the death of Umar (RA) that shall never be filled until the Day of Qiyaamah."

Hadhrat Abu Waa'il reports, "Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once came to us and was given the news of Hadhrat Umar (RA)'s death. I have never seen him weep more than that day and never saw him more depressed. He then said, 'By Allaah! I would have even loved a dog if I knew that Umar loved it. By Allaah! I am certain that even the thorny trees are distressed by the death of Umar (RA).'"[^2]
